page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-32 is a compute-focused instance within the general-purpose virtual machine family. The instance is built on the x86_64 processor architecture and provides 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of system memory. This configuration maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, yielding exactly 2.0 GB of memory per processing core. The instance includes no bundled GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Storage is not bundled locally on the n4d-highcpu-32, meaning the instance lacks integrated local SSD or NVMe disks. All persistent file systems, root volumes, and scratch spaces require attached network block storage. In terms of resource allocation, the machine emphasizes core density over large memory footprints. By limiting RAM to 2.0 GB per core, the hardware configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency for organizations that demand multi-core processing power without paying for surplus memory capacity that would otherwise sit idle.

The balance of 32 dedicated compute cores and 64.0 GB of memory makes the n4d-highcpu-32 applicable to high-throughput compute tasks. Primary workload fits include continuous integration and automated build systems, code compilation, video encoding, microservices hosting, and parallel batch data processing jobs where memory requirements remain moderate.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-32 is an x86_64 architecture virtual server configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory. Operating with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core, this configuration prioritizes compute throughput while reducing memory allocation overhead compared to standard balanced instances. The platform features no integrated local storage and no hardware accelerators, operating without bundled GPUs and without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Persistent storage volumes must be attached externally over the cloud network to support operating system and workload data. The streamlined memory-to-core proportion offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads focused on multi-threaded compute density rather than large in-memory databases. Appropriate deployments include distributed compute jobs, continuous integration and build pipelines, batch data processing, web serving, and parallel algorithmic execution that operates within a moderate memory envelope.
